channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Citi’s Fraser on China's AI 'Enthusiasm'
item.description: Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser says sentiment towards artificial intelligence is noticeably more positive in China than in the US, pointing to differences highlighted during the recent US election and the potential to integrate AI with China's areas of strengths including manufacturing. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: WuXi AppTec Removed From Pentagon’s Chinese Military Firms List
item.description: WuXi AppTec Co. has been removed from the US government’s list of Chinese military companies, relieving the pharmaceutical services contractor of the restrictions and reputational damage tied to the designation.
item.dc:creator: Amber Tong

item.title: India Speaks With Russia, Ukraine Ahead of US-Led Peace Talks
item.description: India held high-level discussions with Russia and Ukraine as New Delhi seeks a more active role in efforts to end their war, ahead of a new round of US-brokered peace talks set to start Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Jon Herskovitz

item.title: North Korea Plans New Torpedo Deployment Next Year in Naval Push
item.description: North Korea said it has tested a new high-speed torpedo that it plans to deploy early next year, extending a recent run of weapons tests ahead of President Donald Trump’s planned Asia trip next week.
item.dc:creator: Soo-Hyang Choi

item.title: Democrats Weigh Using Shutdown Leverage Over Iran War
item.description: Democrats are weighing whether to use an upcoming government funding deadline to pressure President Donald Trump over the war in Iran, with some representatives exploring legislative tactics to restrict military spending. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: How a Bank Collapse Brought Down a President
item.description: Paraguay was supposed to be South America’s safe bet, with fast growth, low inflation and the confidence of international investors. So how did the collapse of Ueno Bank turn into a national crisis? (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Canada Expands US Tariff Exemptions, Cuts Some Aluminum Relief
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney’s government is changing the rules for importers, allowing them to apply for exemptions from Canadian tariffs on a wider range of US goods while ending relief on some American-made aluminum products.
item.dc:creator: Mathieu Dion

item.title: Articles of Impeachment Introduced Against Hegseth
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Rep. Carlos Gimenez (R-FL) says the China Select Committee needs answers about the exact nature of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s relationship and calls it “a breach of national security at a pretty high level.” Sen. Alan Armstrong (R-OK) says permitting reform would provide a long-term, durable fix for building infrastructure and connecting lower-cost energy resources to consumers, but cautions it is not an immediate solution to affordability. Marc Short, former Chief of Staff to former Vice President Mike Pence, says President Donald Trump is “terrific at changing headlines” and says announcing Stephen Miller as White House Chief of Staff helped turn the page from Republicans’ midterm losses. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Short Says Huang China Trip Would Be a Big Mistake
item.description: Marc Short, former Chief of Staff to former Vice President Mike Pence, says President Donald Trump is “terrific at changing headlines” and says announcing Stephen Miller as White House Chief of Staff helped turn the page from Republicans’ midterm losses. Short says politics on both sides will make bipartisan deals difficult even where the Trump administration’s economic policies overlap with positions held by Sens. Bernie Sanders and Elizabeth Warren. Short calls Vice President JD Vance’s post-election analysis “foolish” and says it “diminishes his role,” arguing the administration should instead focus on how it will address voters’ concerns. Short calls the revelations involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang “shocking” and says China was successful in getting the administration to change its position on export controls, adding that he expects congressional investigations. He speaks with Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Sen. Armstrong Says Time Is of the Essence on Permitting
item.description: Sen. Alan Armstrong (R-OK) says permitting reform would provide a long-term, durable fix for building infrastructure and connecting lower-cost energy resources to consumers, but cautions it is not an immediate solution to affordability. Sen. Armstrong says time is of the essence to pass the bipartisan bill during the lame-duck session after years of debate. Sen. Armstrong says he is not concerned by President Donald Trump’s comment that he would not sign a permitting bill with wind turbine components because the legislation is source-neutral and does not favor wind, solar or gas. He speaks with Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rep. Gimenez Says Nvidia Affair Raises Security Concerns
item.description: Rep. Carlos Gimenez (R-FL) says the China Select Committee needs answers about the exact nature of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s relationship and calls it “a breach of national security at a pretty high level.” Rep. Gimenez says he is “probably a no” on the articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth unless something comes to light, arguing Hegseth was carrying out orders from the President. Rep. Gimenez says immigration enforcement has gone “a little too far” and says Congress should pursue comprehensive immigration reform before the lame-duck session ends. He speaks with Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Top Senate Democrat Takes Aim at Epstein’s Wall Street
item.description: The incoming Democratic chairman of the Senate Finance Committee signaled three major banks with ties to disgraced financier Jeffrey Epstein would be top investigative targets for the panel when his party takes control next year.
item.dc:creator: Caitlin Reilly

item.title: Markets Surge as Nvidia Slides on Jensen Huang Scrutiny
item.description: The Close brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are Citi Wealth Head of Portfolio Construction & Analytics Olaolu Aganga, Former Federal Reserve Governor Betsy Duke, Citigroup Managing Director Jason Bazinet, CVS Heath CEO & Chairman David Joyner, Morgan Stanley Head of Wealth Management Jed Finn, Bokeh Capital Partners Founder & CIO Kim Forrest, Seaport Research Partners Senior Analyst David Joyce, Gerber Kawasaki Wealth & Investment Management President & CEO Ross Gerber, Yale School of Management Lecturer of Management Practice Gautam Mukunda, & Dutch Bros CEO Christine Barone. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily Podcast: China’s 25 Year Rise
item.description:
The people, companies and trends shaping the global economy. Watch Carol and Tim LIVE every day on YouTube: http://bit.ly/3vTiACF
Nvidia’s investigation into Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy raises a series of once-unthinkable questions, including whether the man at the center of the AI boom is at risk of losing his job. Nvidia makes chips that are crucial to AI computing equipment and is one of the world’s most valuable businesses. Turmoil within the company risks reverberating through the broader industry.
On today’s episode:
Ian King, Bloomberg News US Semiconductor Reporter Elizabeth Saunders, Professor of Political Science at Columbia University Rachel Metz, Bloomberg News AI Reporter Lynn Martin, NYSE Group President (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Stands By Nvidia's Huang and Defense Secretary Hegseth
item.description: President Donald Trump calls Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang "an amazing guy" and offers support for Pete Hegseth. Tyler Kendall reports on "Balance of Power: Evening Edition." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bloomberg Opinion’s Gautam Mukunda on Nvidia Probe
item.description: Gautam Mukunda said Nvidia's reported breach appears serious, but routine espionage by both the US and China is an established feature of their relationship. He argued that a more significant concern is evidence that Nvidia chips have reached China in violation of export controls. He speaks with Vonnie Quinn on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Betsy Duke on Post-Midterms Inflation Outlook
item.description: Ahead of the October CPI report, Betsy Duke said the data is unlikely to alter the Federal Reserve’s policy direction. She argued that labor-market and economic indicators show no weakness the Fed needs to guard against, and that interest rates do not yet appear restrictive. Duke said fiscal policy and supply-side factors have contributed substantially to inflation, but the Fed remains responsible for controlling it and should act amid public frustration over persistent price increases. She speaks with Vonnie Quinn & Scarlet Fu on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Says FBI Is Reviewing Huang Affair, Cites Call With CEO
item.description: President Donald Trump said the FBI is looking into Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang’s extramarital relationship with a suspected Chinese spy, and offered his support to the embattled chip magnate a day after the affair was disclosed.
item.dc:creator: Skylar Woodhouse

item.title: Trump Signals Further Airstrikes on Iran Won’t Be Necessary
item.description: President Donald Trump said further strikes on Iran wouldn’t be necessary but the US remains “locked and loaded,” an indication that he’s winding down the conflict after Republicans’ midterm elections loss underscored its deep unpopularity.
item.dc:creator: Jeff Mason

item.title: DOJ Civil Division Head Is Latest to Resign After Midterms
item.description: Brett Shumate, the head of the Justice Department’s civil division, has resigned, according to US Attorney General Todd Blanche.
item.dc:creator: Jimmy Jenkins, Chris Strohm and Zoe Tillman
